title: Congruence and bounded centers for adic formal blowup systems
statement: Use the Noetherian adic formal systems and their affine charts, completions and formal blowups of [def-per-noetherian-adic-formal-system], with $F_n$ the reduction modulo the $(n+1)$st power of the specified ideal of definition. For morphisms $f,g:G\to F$, define congruence at precision $m\geq0$ by $f_n=g_n$ for every $n+1\leq m$; precision zero is vacuous. A morphism is adic when each square formed by it and a transition $n\leq k$ is cartesian. A center $J_n$ has exponent $e\geq0$ if on every formal affine chart with coordinate ring $A$ and ideal of definition $I$ it is induced at every order by an ideal $H\subseteq A$ containing $I^e$. The distinguished ideal is locally principal regular when every point has a formal affine chart with ideal generated by a non-zero-divisor. A morphism of affine completion systems induces a specified ring map $\varphi:A\to B$ when at each order its composite with the canonical closed immersion into $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is the canonical immersion into $\operatorname{Spec}B$ followed by $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$. The affine blowup system for $(A,I,H)$ is the completion of $\operatorname{Bl}_H\operatorname{Spec}A$ along the extended ideal $I$. Its projection is characterized by the equations into $\operatorname{Spec}A$ at every order. A finite precision tower has $r+1$ such Noetherian locally principal regular formal systems, $r$ formal blowup arrows, their ordered centers, and exponents bounding those centers; $r=0$ is allowed. A map of towers consists of adic level maps commuting with the arrows and identifying the centers. Such a map is a flat formal pullback when each level map is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] at every infinitesimal order and each square with a blowup arrow is cartesian. Unit center ideals have exponent zero and empty center, and are retained.
